sampling_model.design: Condition on fixed supplied nuisance fits. The observed experiment consists only of three mutually independent evaluation folds with projected law \(Q_P=P^n\otimes P^n\otimes P^n\). Every median-of-means statistic uses \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty near-equal consecutive blocks; the coverage and frontier claims apply for \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\).
sampling_model.units: Each fold contains \(n\) independent superpopulation observations \(Z_i=(X_i,T_i,Y_i)\).
sampling_model.treatment: Continuous treatment obeying \(T=g_0(X)+\eta\), with \(\eta\perp X\) and \(E_P[\eta^2]=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Known unit treatment-residual variance is the nondegeneracy normalization.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The statistical law class contains only primitive laws. The selected training-realized functions are external fixed inputs, and uniformity is over all supplied pairs in \(\mathcal H_n(P)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 3.2 and 5.4 give a Gaussian DML lower bound and a fixed-positive-cumulant ACE point-estimation upper bound on separate classes.
Theorem 1 and Proposition 2 characterize expected-length adaptation over unions in Gaussian linear-functional experiments.
The paper obtains composite-hypothesis lower bounds by moment-matched priors and chi-square control of normal mixtures.
Theorem 5 rules out second-order PLM orthogonality under Gaussian residuals, while Theorems 8--10 construct higher-order moments under non-Gaussian residuals.
Theorem 2 establishes coverage and interval-length control for the filtered union, while Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient.

body.tldr: For a primitive JMS partially linear law and fixed training-realized nuisance fits supplied within stated \(L^8(P_X)\) radii, one interval is honest over exact-Gaussian and shrinking fourth-cumulant-separated branches of the projected evaluation experiment. Four explicit Bonferroni-calibrated median-of-means events use nonempty finite-sample block partitions and cover safe DML, four residual moments, centered Appell inversion, and its empirical slope. The non-Gaussian finite-sample length is \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n+d_np_{\mathrm{sel},n}\}\), with an explicit bound on \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\), and reduces to \(\min\{d_n,B_n/\delta_n\}\) when \(\delta_n/s_n\to\infty\). The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\), with conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy confined to its lower subexperiment. The proved contribution is the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier; the sibling repository paper treats fixed-separation spectral estimation, while the fuzzy-Hermite branchwise converse and removal of the Gaussian logarithm remain labelled open-ended questions.

project_justification.gap: Published structure-agnostic PLM theory and the sibling repository paper study separate Gaussian or fixed-non-Gaussian point-estimation classes and fixed-separation spectral constructions, not one conditionally specified projected experiment with union honesty, shrinking cumulant separation, and branchwise expected length.
project_justification.niche: The informative object is the two-coordinate expected-length region; the global union supremum remains governed by the Gaussian coordinate.
project_justification.fill: The proved component combines explicit nonempty-block four-event calibration, a finite-sample branch-selection error envelope, a safe unnormalized DML interval, and a fully centered split Appell inversion for the shrinking-separation upper frontier. Conditional outcome-noise nondegeneracy is auxiliary to the Gaussian expected-length lower theorem, and the PLM-compatible fuzzy-Hermite converse remains open.

body.related_work: Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis, especially Theorems 3.2 and 5.4 and Appendices D and G, inform the Gaussian lower coordinate and fixed-separation ACE component but do not give a union-honest shrinking-cumulant interval. The auxiliary condition \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) is not attributed to their envelope and is used only for the Gaussian expected-length lower subexperiment. Mackey, Syrgkanis, and Zadik, Theorems 5 and 8--10, inform the Gaussian obstruction and higher-order score. Cai and Low, Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, inform branchwise expected length, while their Gaussian model has no learned PLM residual. Cai and Low's 2011 Hermite mixture method informs the fuzzy-prior handle. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman inform localized product-mixture calculations. Chernozhukov et al. supply the split DML benchmark. Zheng, Bonvini, and Guo's Theorem 2 informs filtered-union coverage and interval-length control, while their Theorem 3 supplies the oracle-proximity and existence ingredient; neither theorem uses treatment cumulants. The sibling repository paper \(\texttt{stat\_sa\_plm\_cumulant\_converse}\) proves fixed-separation spectral and estimation constructions and explicitly leaves shrinking separation, adaptive switching, uniform inference, and a local matching lower bound unresolved. The present proved contribution is instead the conditional supplied-fit shrinking-separation upper frontier; it does not claim a matching Pareto frontier. Quessy and Mailhot analyze centered and studentized normality statistics without nuisance-contaminated residuals. Armstrong, Kline, and Sun motivate caution about pretesting for a different point-risk object.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The certified Gaussian lower coordinate is \(d_n^-\), not \(d_n\), and uses the auxiliary nondegenerate Gaussian subclass \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\). The upper theorem neither needs the conditional outcome-noise variance lower bound nor identifies a matching Pareto boundary. Its finite-sample guarantee starts at \(n=\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\), when every requested calibration block count is available. The early kill test is a finite Rademacher-partition exponential-Hermite pair supported on primitive PLM laws, sharing admissible fixed supplied fits, and inducing projected mixtures with bounded chi-square distance and the target displacements in the open-ended question.
body.honest_scope: The law class is primitive and contains no learner-performance condition. All inference is conditional on fixed supplied fits and uniform over their radius set. The Appell polynomial estimates the first four raw residual moments on a fold independent of inversion. Every median-of-means operator partitions the sample into \(b_n(\beta)=\min\{n,\lceil8\log(2/\beta)\rceil\}\) nonempty blocks, and the theorem assumes \(n\ge\lceil8\log(32/\alpha)\rceil\). Four named events receive error \(\alpha/4\) each, while the separate bound \(p_{\mathrm{sel},n}\) quantifies wrong-branch selection. The novel auxiliary restriction \(E_P[\xi^2\mid X,T]\ge c_{\xi}\) defines only \(\mathcal G_{\xi,n}\) and is used only for the Gaussian expected-length converse, not for the adaptive upper frontier. The sibling repository paper settles fixed-separation spectral estimation, not this local-to-Gaussian union-honest length problem. The branchwise converse and removal of \(\Lambda_n\) are open. No matching Pareto boundary or improvement of global union-supremum expected length is claimed.
